cues.text: Welcome in Jürgen! ... Grab your water, ... grab your towel, and let's do this. One hour today, three ten-minute sweet spot blocks. Nice and easy for now. We're just getting the legs moving.

Let's get the legs moving. Easy pedalling, nice and smooth. Settle into a rhythm enjoy the landscape.... We're doing a sweet spot session today. Keep your water close, and your towel closer. This is going to be a good one.
How are the legs? Don't judge them yet. Give them a few minutes to wake up. Everybody's warm-up feels a little clunky at first.
Get that fan on you. There's no breeze indoors, so make your own. Trust me, you'll thank me in block three.
Keep it easy, keep it honest. The warm-up is not the workout. We're saving the good stuff for later.
Quick word on sweet spot. It sits just under your threshold. Hard enough to build real endurance, controlled enough that we can stack up thirty minutes of it.
Five minutes in. Feel that warmth coming? Head up, shoulders down and away from your ears. Soft grip, a little bend in the elbows. Find your rhythm.
Take a sip. Little and often. Then right back to that easy spin.
Let's check in from the ground up. Feet flat as you push, and think about the whole pedal stroke. Push, pull, all the way round.
Two minutes out. Here's the plan. Three blocks, all the same quality. No hero first block and miserable last one. Steady wins today.
Thirty seconds! Pick a gear that feels good and let the trainer bring the resistance up. No heroics in the first minute. Here it comes.
Here we go, block one! Ten minutes at eighty-eight percent. Strong and controlled, not flat out. Settle in and own it.
Let the trainer find the number. You should feel the work now, with something left in the tank. That's the sweet spot.
This is why we love sweet spot. Thirty minutes of real aerobic work today, and you'll still be able to walk tomorrow.
Breathe. Long and steady. Don't hold your breath when it gets tough. Let it in, let it out.
Picture a long climb. Go too hard at the bottom and it bites you at the top. Ride the whole hill, not just the first bend.
Halfway through block one! Core engaged, chest open, shoulders relaxed. Let the legs do the work. You could hold this for another five, so let's do exactly that.
Every minute here is another brick in your foundation. It doesn't happen in one day. It happens because you keep showing up.
Check in. Can you still say a few words? Good. That's right where we want you.
Two minutes left. Stop chasing every single watt. Watch the trend, not the flicker. Smooth is fast.
Sixty seconds! Same rhythm, same effort, right to the end. Easy minutes are waiting for you.
Block one, done! Nice work. Let the resistance drop, keep the legs turning, grab a drink and dry off. We recover now so the next two are just as good.
Keep spinning. Easy pedalling helps you recover better than stopping. Loose legs, loose shoulders.
Fun fact while we spin. Lactate isn't just waste. Your body actually reuses it as fuel. Pretty clever machine you've got there.
Two minutes. Sip, check the fan, and ask yourself how that first block felt. Controlled? Good. That's the plan.
One minute out. Remember, resistance is always relative to you. If today is a heavy day, it's fine to turn the intensity down a notch. Showing up is what counts.
Thirty seconds. Get ready to pick it up. Same power as before. Nothing to prove, just a job to do.
We're back! Block two, ten minutes. It might feel a little harder than the first, and that's normal. This is where we build the strength to keep the power coming when the legs get tired.
Give it a minute to settle. If it feels awkward, don't spike the cadence. Just breathe and let the rhythm come back.
FTP is a guide, not a magic number. Sleep, stress and heat all change how this feels. Ride what's in front of you today.
No traffic lights, no descents, no freewheeling. Just you and the work. That's the beauty of riding indoors.
Check your face. Clenching your jaw? Let it go. No extra watts come from your teeth.
Five down, five to go! Your heart rate might creep up even though the power hasn't. That's normal. Fan on, relax the grip, keep breathing.
Stay with me. A slow rise in heart rate is fine. But if something feels really wrong, back off. You know your body.
Three minutes. This is patience under load. You don't have to feel amazing every second to ride a great interval.
Two minutes. Give yourself one job. A smooth cadence, or steady breathing. Just one. Nail it.
Last minute of block two! Stick with it. When this one's done, that's twenty minutes of sweet spot in the bank.
Two down, one to go! Big drink, drop those shoulders, let the breathing settle. We want to start the last one ready, not rushed.
Enjoy this. Recovery isn't wasted time. It's what lets you ride the next block with quality.
Fuel note. On longer, harder sessions, carbs help you keep going. For this hour, it mostly depends on what you ate before.
Think about your weekend rides. Repeating a solid effort when you're already tired. That's exactly what we're training right now.
One minute out. The target isn't going up. The challenge is doing it again on tired legs. You've got this.
Thirty seconds to the last block! Legs feeling heavy? Of course they are. Find your rhythm early and take it one minute at a time.
Last one, let's go! Same ten minutes, same power. This is the top of a long climb with kilometres already in your legs. Controlled, steady, strong.
Nine to go. Don't count the seconds. Settle into a cadence you like and give yourself one small job at a time.
Easy rides matter too. Not every day needs to be a sweet spot day. But today it is, so let's finish it well.
Legs heavy? That's fatigue doing its thing, not fitness slipping away. Keep it manageable. Keep it smooth.
Be the smart rider on the climb. Steady pace, no attacking every bend. Nearly halfway.
Five minutes left! Legs talking to you? Answer with good form. Smooth pedal stroke, shoulders down, steady breathing. Just keep chipping away. I'm right here with you.
Four minutes. Consistency is the goal. If it gets unusually hard, back off rather than forcing the number.
Three minutes. Stop staring at the clock. Look up, find that smooth pedal stroke, and ride it.
Two minutes! Almost there. Keep the cadence up so the trainer doesn't wind up on you. And no medals for extra suffering.
Last sixty seconds! Stay with that rhythm. No sprint finish, just a strong, steady one. Finish it the way you started it.
That's it, the hard work is done! Ten minutes to wind it down. Breathe it out and enjoy the easy spin. Thirty minutes of sweet spot. That's real foundation you just built.
Feel how light that is? Enjoy it. Zero need to push now. You earned this.
Let your breathing and heart rate come down on their own. Easy legs, easy mind.
Think back over the three blocks. Did they feel the same, or did the last one bite? Either way, that's useful for next time.
Something worth noticing over the weeks. When the same power starts to feel easier, that's progress you can feel, not just see.
Five minutes left. A clear head is part of what we get out of this too. Away from the noise, just you, your breathing and the road.
Balance these with genuinely easy rides. You can build a lot of fitness without every session hurting.
Three minutes. After the ride, a normal meal with some carbs and protein. Nothing fancy needed.
Two more minutes. If there's another hard day coming, listen to your legs tomorrow. A flexible plan is a smart plan.
Last minute. Easy spin all the way home. Well, we're already home, but you know what I mean.

finish.text: And that's a wrap! You showed up, you did the work, and that's how the foundation gets built. Grab some water, get something to eat, and let those legs recover. See you next ride!

intro.text: Let's look at your heart rate.
Quick check on the heart rate.

high.text: A touch higher than I'd like. Keep breathing steadily.

too_high.text: Watch your heart rate, slow it down a bit.
That's high. Ease off a little and let it come down.

good.text: This is great, keep it up.
Spot on. Keep doing exactly that.

high.text: That's a bit over the target. Ease off slightly.

low.text: That's a little under the target. Push just a bit more.

power_high.text: A little hot! Ease back and let the trainer settle.
Easy, tiger. No bonus points for extra watts today. Keep it smooth.
Bring it back to the target. Steady rhythm, no surges.

power_low.text: Just under the target. Keep those pedals turning and let the trainer catch up.
Power's dipped. Find your rhythm again, nice and smooth.
A little below. If the legs are cooked today, it's okay to lower the intensity.

cadence_high.text: Legs are spinning quick! Bring the cadence down a touch.
Slow the legs a little. Smooth and controlled.

cadence_low.text: Cadence is dropping. Lift it back up before it gets heavy.
Quicker legs! If it's too heavy, turn the target down.

on_target.text: That's it! Right in the sweet spot. Love it.
Spot on. Keep doing exactly what you're doing.
